about: The far ring's landmarks (docs/design/world-squares.md section 4 and its "On paper (2026-11-09)" notes; Chem.FarLandmarks): for each kind of landmark the plan places that shows from far off, how far it's seen and roughly how big it is. Keyed by type: a village intent's form's "landmark" ("great tree", "volcano", "lake"), a port on an inland sea ("port"), the plan's "castle" and "spire", an outcrop's kind and a waystation's ("inn", "shop"). A type not here (a cave, a sea view, a crossing) isn't a far landmark: it's drawn as part of the land when its chunk is known. "seenFrom" is a radius in chunks from the character, at least sim.json's streaming.know + 2 so a landmark shows past the known ring. It sets the landmark's own haze (FarLand.shader): past sight, 1 - 10^-((d / seenFrom)^2), 90% at seenFrom, and it goes wholly into the sky over the last chunk and a half, so a landmark reads at about 50-75% haze out to three quarters of its seenFrom and is gone at it. The big ones are seen well past where they stand from the spawn (the nine's volcano is 13 chunks from it: 72% at 18, 94% at 14), the castle and the great tree from about 9 chunks (73% and 67%), the small ones only near; "height" (above the ground at it) and "radius" are metres, and "shape" is the stand-in far mesh's profile (cone, crater, needle, tree, dome, keep: a flat-topped block), as the paper prototype's Horizon panel draws them. The volcano's size is its stamp's (village-with-landmark.json: a cone 64-76 cells across the radius, 55-65 m high), so it doesn't change size as its chunks come into the known ring; the rest are the paper's stand-ins. A row's "far" is how its far mesh is drawn where it can no longer have given way to its chunk's land (FarRing.StretchFrom: sight + 1 chunks on a diagonal, about 680 m, coming in whole 3 chunks on), so it's its true size wherever it meets the land and never pops: "stretch" times as tall (the volcano's true 60 m is under 3 degrees from the valley at 1.2 km, a mound behind the nearer hills, so far off it stands 108 m, about its stamp's own slope near the rim), a "notch" in its rim facing the eye of that part of its height (a crater, which a turned profile can't show from the side), and an "apron" of land out to that many times its radius and down to the water, since past the known ring no land is drawn under it. View data only: nothing shared reads it, and it isn't in the map's hash.
